title: Ronaldo retirement date 'revealed' as fans may not get to see him in UK again
summary: Reports say Cristiano Ronaldo will end his international career after Portugal's Nations League match against Wales on September 24 at Sporting Lisbon's Jose Alvalade. The 41-year-old, Portugal's record scorer and appearance holder, now plays for Al-Nassr and is unlikely to play again in the UK except possibly in a friendly.
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from international football has reportedly been revealed by journalist Mohammed Awaad.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner, now 41, rose to global prominence during a six-year spell with Manchester United before moving on to Real Madrid, Juventus and most recently Al-Nassr. He has been a mainstay of the Portugal team for more than two decades.

According to the report, Ronaldo will make one more appearance for Portugal — their next fixture, a Nations League match against Wales on September 24. That game is expected to be staged at the Jose Alvalade stadium, home of his boyhood club Sporting Lisbon.

If the plan holds, the outing would likely be his final match in a Portugal shirt and would make it unlikely he will be seen again in front of UK crowds during competitive international football. His club career in Saudi Arabia with Al-Nassr also reduces the chances of frequent matches against British teams, leaving only pre-season friendlies as the most probable route for another UK appearance.

Ronaldo featured in his sixth World Cup finals tournament in the most recent edition but once again did not secure the World Cup trophy. He remains Portugal's record goalscorer, with 146 goals in 233 appearances, three of which were scored at the latest World Cup.

He made his Portugal debut in 2003, coming on as a substitute for Luis Figo in a 1-0 win over Kazakhstan. His international record of 233 caps is the highest in men's football, ahead of Lionel Messi on 207; the article notes that USA women's legend Kristine Lilly holds an overall record of 354 international appearances.

Ronaldo has helped Portugal to major honours in recent years. The nation claimed the European Championship and lifted the Nations League trophy on multiple occasions, with the article citing victories including a Euros win and Nations League successes.

He has a previous competitive meeting with Wales, from Euro 2016, when he scored a header and assisted Nani in a 2-0 victory in Lyon. That history underlines the symbolic nature of a final Portugal appearance against Wales at Sporting's ground.

While the report frames the September fixture as his last international outing, there is still speculation that he could attempt to continue to Euro 2028 or even the 2030 World Cup. The latest account, however, points to a sooner end to his Portugal career.

Ronaldo's club and international legacy remains significant: a record goalscorer and appearance leader for Portugal, a six-time World Cup participant, and one of football's most recognisable figures. The suggested farewell at the Jose Alvalade would bring his international journey full circle, returning to the stadium associated with his early days at Sporting Lisbon.
